_note: Stage D: the office sequences S1-S6 (v4 section 3). Answer keys live here; the game never shows them directly.

body.name: Cornelius Pryce
body.text: Cornelius Pryce sits slumped over his desk, one hand still near his glass. His face is flushed pink, not the grey you'd expect.
body.note: Pryce's face is pink, not grey.

decanter.name: Brandy decanter and glass
decanter.text: A cut-glass decanter, a third full, and a single glass with a little brandy left in the bottom. There's a faint bitter smell, like crushed almonds.
decanter.note: The brandy smells faintly of bitter almonds.

musicbox.name: Music box
musicbox.text: A little walnut music box. Its comb teeth are numbered 1 to 8 in pencil. The key has been wound recently: there is still tension in the spring. On the brass winding key, under your lens, a smudged fingerprint: small and narrow, far too small for Pryce's big hands.
musicbox.note: The music box was wound recently. A small, narrow fingerprint on its key: not Pryce's.

calendar.name: Desk calendar
calendar.text: Saturday 18 November is circled hard, twice. In Pryce's hand: END IT.
calendar.note: Pryce's calendar for today says END IT.

blotter.name: Blotter
blotter.text: Rubbed with pencil, the indent of the last thing he wrote comes up: ZÜRICH 0500 / 2 PASS.

note.name: Typed note under the door
note.text: Typed on yellow paper and pushed under the door: 'Five hundred by Saturday or the papers get the real Marigold weather report. You know I kept a copy.' No signature. The letter 'e' is chipped throughout.
note.note: A typed demand note was pushed under the door: five hundred by Saturday. The 'e' is chipped.

revolver.name: Desk drawer
revolver.text: A revolver lies in the drawer: all six chambers loaded, the barrel clean and cold. It hasn't been fired.
revolver.note: The revolver in the drawer is fully loaded and has not been fired.

watch.name: Pocket watch
watch.text: Pryce's gold pocket watch lies by the blotter. It stopped at seventeen minutes past three. Engraved inside the lid: 'The minute the sky stopped.'
watch.note: His pocket watch stopped at 3:17. 'The minute the sky stopped.'

photo.name: Photograph
photo.text: A girl in a flying jacket laughs in front of a big three-engined plane. Written under it: 'My girl, nineteen today. The Marigold, May 1931.'
photo.note: Photo: 'My girl, nineteen today.' The plane behind her has three engines.

book.name: Hollow book
book.text: One book is lighter than it should be: it's hollow. Inside, a card in Pryce's hand: 'Left, her years. Right, the wings' hearts. Left, the minute the sky stopped.'
book.note: Safe riddle: left, her years; right, the wings' hearts; left, the minute the sky stopped.

stove.name: Stove and flue
stove.text: The stove is cold. Its pipe is barely ten centimetres across. Nothing bigger than a cat goes through that.

window.name: Barred window
window.text: Iron bars set deep in mortar, and the dust on the sill is unbroken. Nobody has been through here.

bolt.name: Door bolt
bolt.text: A heavy brass bolt, thrown from the inside. You try to work it from outside with a thread through the gap over the door: the thread slips off every time.

ceiling.name: Ceiling
ceiling.text: Tongue-and-groove boards, nailed tight, with an undisturbed film of dust in every joint.

vent.name: Floor vent
vent.text: A small iron grille, twenty centimetres by ten. Too small for a person, but you feel a cold draught rising through it. From where?
vent.note: A cold draught comes up through the office floor vent.

floor.name: The floor
floor.text: You kneel and knock across the boards. Solid... solid... and then, under the rug, a hollow knock.
floor.note: The floor sounds hollow under the rug.

cable.name: A cable in the shaft
cable.prompt: Look at the cable in the shaft
cable.text: A thick black telegraph cable comes out of the joists and runs down the corner of the shaft. A third of the way down, someone has cut into it and spliced on a thinner, newer wire, wrapped with small, careful twists of tape. The new wire runs on down into the dark.
cable.note: The telegraph cable in the trapdoor shaft has a newer wire spliced onto it, running down.

S1.title: Walk the Room
S1.intro: Before anything is moved, test every way in or out of this room, and photograph what matters. You have 12 camera plates: not enough for everything in the room, so choose.
S1.platesNote: You don't need a photo of everything, only of what matters to the case. Run out, and Danny has spare boxes at HQ.

spareBox.label: Fetch a spare box of plates from HQ (20 min)
spareBox.got: Danny sends over a fresh box: {n} more plates. Every photo you've taken is kept.

S1.notExamined: You haven't examined this yet. Find it in the room first (E).
S1.wrong: Danny frowns at your sheet. "Chief, one of these doesn't add up. Have another look."
S1.done: Every way in or out is accounted for, and the important things are on film.
S1.missingPhotos: Still not on film: {list}. Anything not in your list above hasn't been examined yet: find it in the room and press E on it first.
S1.noPlates: You're out of plates. Fetch a spare box from HQ (the button below): it adds 12 more, and keeps every photo you've taken.

S2.title: The Body
S2.intro: Doctor Lindqvist examines the body while you direct him. He is sure it was heart failure. Mark each sign: does it fit a heart attack, or not?

areas.name: Eyes
areas.doc: Pupils dilated. Quite normal after death.

areas.name: Skin
areas.doc: A little flushed. The heat of the stove, I expect.
areas.see: His skin is a healthy pink, almost rosy. The stove has been cold all night.

areas.name: Mouth and breath
areas.doc: Nothing of note. Brandy, of course.
areas.see: Under the brandy, a faint smell of bitter almonds.

areas.name: Hands
areas.doc: Clenched. The pain of the attack.

areas.name: Fingernails
areas.see: The nail beds are pink, not blue.

areas.name: Stiffness (rigor)
areas.doc: Fully stiff. He has been dead for some hours.
areas.see: The jaw and limbs are fully rigid.

areas.name: Settled blood (lividity)
areas.doc: Where the blood has settled. Perfectly ordinary.
areas.see: The settled blood is a bright cherry red, not the usual purple.

areas.name: Chest
areas.doc: No marks. No wounds. A heart, giving out.

S2.wrong: Lindqvist looks relieved. "You see? Nothing unusual there." (That one fits a heart attack.)
S2.done: Pink skin, pink nails, cherry-red settled blood and bitter almonds. That isn't a heart attack. Lindqvist has gone very pale.

S3.title: Time of Death
S3.intro: Work out about what time he died. A body cools about 1.5°F an hour from the normal 98.6°F. Stiffness and settled blood must agree with your answer. Set the time on the slider.
S3.label: He died at about
facts: Normal body temperature: 98.6°F. Cooling: about 1.5°F per hour (the stove was cold).
Stiffness: complete. That takes six to twelve hours.
Settled blood: fixed, does not move when pressed. That takes eight hours or more.

check._note: Any answer within 'within' minutes of 'answer' is right (the cooling rate is only 'about' 1.5 degrees an hour).

S3.wrong: Danny runs the numbers on his pad. "Chief, that time doesn't fit the thermometer. Try again."
S3.done: He died around twenty to ten last night, before ten o'clock. So who was playing the music box at ten?

S4.title: The Bench Test
S4.intro: Doctor Lindqvist's field kit: three test chemicals (A, B, C) and enough for six drops. Test the samples. You'll need the chart that says what each chemical shows.

chartRoutes.label: Ask Doctor Lindqvist for his chart (5 min)
chartRoutes.ok: He hesitates, then hands it over. "Keep it away from the... from my other patient," he murmurs, and then won't say who he means.
chartRoutes.no: "I, er, seem to have mislaid it." He won't meet your eye.

chartRoutes.label: Use Danny's reference book (15 min)
chartRoutes.ok: Danny finds the table in his chemistry manual and copies it out for you.

chartRoutes.label: Prise the kit's lid open and find it yourself (2 min, Lindqvist won't like it)
chartRoutes.ok: The chart was in the lid all along. Lindqvist stiffens.

chart: A: turns green with sugar (useless here).
B: turns deep 'Prussian' blue with cyanide.
C: turns brown with plant alkaloids, like digitalis heart drops.
S4.question: Which samples held the poison?
S4.refill: Danny can fetch a fresh vial from the doctor's room (30 min).
S4.wrong: That doesn't match your results, Chief.
S4.done: Cyanide, in the brandy decanter and his glass. Not his tonic, not his heart drops. Someone poisoned the decanter.

S5.title: The Safe
S5.intro: A heavy safe with a dial from 0 to 39. Three numbers: left, right, left.
S5.dialRange: The dial only goes from 0 to 39.

drill.label: Drill it open (60 min, loud, may damage papers)
drill.note: Drilling scorched the papers inside: the letter is half lost.

contents.name: A half-burnt letter
contents.text: "...tomorrow I end the silence. I have kept it too long and it has cost too much. Forgive me, my girl, and forgive me for the years..." The rest is charred.

contents.name: Maintenance log, torn corner
contents.text: The Marigold's log, May 1931. Engine mount No. 2: 'Hairline crack, monitor.' Below it, in another hand: 'Passed. A. Brennan.' The corner with the next entry is torn away.

contents.name: Bank stubs
contents.text: Cheque stubs: two hundred dollars a month for two years, each initialled 'T.Q.'

contents.name: Meridian Air envelope
contents.text: Meridian Air letterhead. A carbon of the 1931 accident inquiry's last page, and a note: 'Signature attended to. J.F-B.' The weather report clipped to it reads 'Clear by noon'.

S5.done: The safe is open. Four things inside, and every one of them is somebody's motive.

S6.title: The Floor, the Box and the Latch
S6.intro: Listen to the music box. Its comb teeth are numbered 1 to 8, and the bookshelf has eight pull-books. Pull the books in the order the tune plays.
S6.needsKnock: You don't know what you're looking for yet. Maybe check the floor first.
S6.wrongBook: Clunk. The books slide back. Wrong order.

crowbar.label: Crowbar the floorboards (15 min, very loud)

S6.done: A latch clicks under the floor. The rug sags: there is a trapdoor beneath it, and a breath of cold air comes up from the dark. A black cable runs down one corner of the shaft.
S6.trapdoor: A trapdoor, and iron rungs going down into the dark. Far below, somebody has left a lamp burning.

S23.title: The Prints
S23.intro: Fingerprints lifted in the office, under the lab lamp. First get comparison prints from everyone, then match each lifted print: pattern, width (use the callipers) and scars.
S23.needsText: You need to bag the decanter, glass and music box first. Walk the room (S1) in the office.

collect.label: Ask everyone for their prints, openly (20 min, they won't like it)
collect.text: Everyone grumbles and rolls their fingers on the card. Billie bristles at being measured.

collect.label: Lift them quietly from last night's dinner glasses (35 min)
collect.text: Ox stacked last night's dinner glasses by the sink and never washed them. Each one is still by its owner's place card.

lifted.name: Print from the music box key

S23.measureFirst: Measure it with the callipers first.
S23.wrong: Danny holds the two cards side by side. "They don't match, Chief. Look at the pattern, the width and the scars."
S23.done: The decanter and the music box carry the same print: small, narrow, the ridges smoothed by old burns. It belongs to nobody at that dinner. Billie's hands are scarred too, but three millimetres wider.

S25.title: The Timeline
S25.intro: Pin last night's events on the time strip in the order they happened. You can only pin what you've actually learned. Fixed points: the bolt was thrown at 21:25, the tune was heard at 22:00, the door was broken down at 06:10.

cards.text: 19:00 Dinner in the mess hall; Pryce's toast
22:00 The music box is heard through the bolted door
About 22:45 A bang: a backfire, not a shot
After 23:15 A typed demand note is pushed under the door
06:10 Billie breaks the door down; the bolt is still thrown

S25.missing: You can't finish the strip yet: some events are still unknown. Talk to people and keep investigating.
S25.wrong: The strip won't hold: something is out of order. Remember, nobody can be in two places, and the bolt stayed thrown from 21:25 until 06:10.
S25.done: The night holds together: the room was bolted at 21:25, he died soon after, and someone wound the music box at ten in a locked room.

smokepot.name: Flare and smoke pots
smokepot.text: A row of old runway flare pots, and a crate of smoke pots used to show pilots the wind. You take one.

ventstack.name: Culvert vent stack
ventstack.text: A short rusted pipe sticking out of the gravel, capped with a cowl. Warm air breathes out of it, steady as a sleeper. Underneath: the old fuel-line culvert.
ventstack.note: A rusty vent pipe in the fuel farm yard breathes warm air.

ventstack_light.prompt: Light a smoke pot in the vent stack (5 min)
ventstack_light.text: You drop the lit smoke pot into the cowl. Thick grey smoke pours down into the culvert. You have about forty minutes before it's gone: see where it comes out.
ventstack_light.lit: The smoke is going down. Go and see where it comes out!

smoke_hangar.name: Office floor vent
smoke_hangar.text: Grey smoke is curling up through the little floor vent in Pryce's office. The culvert runs right under this room.

smoke_storage.name: Storage shed floor
smoke_storage.text: Smoke is seeping up between two floorboards along a straight seam, as if around the edge of a hatch.

smoke_darkroom.name: Darkroom storeroom
smoke_darkroom.text: Behind the chemical shelves, smoke leaks out of a crack where the floor meets the wall. The floorboards there are scuffed.

walks.smoke_none: No smoke here. Either it hasn't arrived, or this place isn't connected.

radio.name: Hobbs's radio desk
radio.prompt: Hobbs's radio and the telegram tape

posts.name: Conduit marker post
posts.text: A short rusty post stamped 'G.P.O. CABLE'. Another stands a few paces further on, and another: they march away across the runway.

splice.name: Splice box
splice.text: An iron junction box half buried by the maintenance shed. Inside, the old telegraph cable has a newer wire spliced onto it with careful, small hands. The new wire runs on toward the hangar.

cableend.name: Where the cable goes under
cableend.prompt: Follow the wire to the hangar wall
cableend.text: The spliced wire dives into a conduit pipe at the foot of the hangar wall, heading under the floor. Toward the office.

rack.name: Drying rack
rack.text: Ox's drying rack in the kitchen: two cups and two plates, washed and set to dry, though he lives alone in the shed. Hobbs says it's the same every night.
rack.note: Two cups and two plates on Ox's drying rack every night.

crates.name: Stacked crates
crates.prompt: The crates and the marks in the dust (S15)

hatch.name: Hatch in the back room
hatch.text: A square hatch in the floor of the little back room, with a fresh rope handle. Cold air comes up around it. This is where Ox brings his trays.

newspaper.name: A newspaper from 1931
newspaper.text: Pinned above the HQ desk, Danny's cutting from the Reno Evening Gazette, 16 May 1931: 'MARIGOLD LOST ON RAVEN RIDGE. Six aboard; five bodies recovered. Search for Miss C. Pryce, 19, abandoned.' Six aboard. Five bodies.
newspaper.note: 1931 newspaper: six aboard the Marigold, only five bodies recovered.

S17.title: The Smoke Test
S17.done: Smoke from one pipe at the fuel farm came up in the hangar office, the storage shed and the darkroom. Danny whistles. "Chief, the whole field is hollow."

S18.title: Follow the Wire
S18.intro: The telegram that brought you here was sent from this line. Here is its tape. Play each operator's sending and find the one that matches the tape's rhythm: speed, evenness, and the little hitch in the Q.
S18.wrong: Look at the tapes side by side. Is it as fast? As even? Does it stumble on the Q in the same place?
S18.matched: It's the unknown sender: slow, perfectly even, and copying Hobbs's stumble on the Q, like someone who learned by listening. Now follow the wire: the cable runs under the runway, and the iron posts mark where.
S18.done: The telegraph line was tapped near the maintenance shed, and the tap runs under the hangar. Whoever sent the telegram did it from somewhere under the airfield.

S14.title: The Ration Stores
S14.intro: The storage shed's ration ledger against the mess roster. Work out the difference for each day: rations signed out minus people actually fed.
S14.signed: Every extra ration is initialled 'A.B.': Abel Brennan. Ox.

pages.label: November 1931
pages.text: The extra ration starts on 16 November 1931. Before that, the numbers match.

S14.question: Since when has someone been signing out an extra ration?
options: Since 16 November 1931, six months after the crash
S14.wrong: Check your sums against the roster, Chief.
S14.wrongStart: Turn back through the ledger to the first page where the numbers stop matching.
S14.done: One extra ration, every single day, for two years, signed out by Ox. Somebody on this airfield is being fed who isn't on any roster.

S15.title: The Marks in the Dust
S15.intro: Curved scuffs in the dust show where these crates usually sit. Push them back onto the marks (you can push a crate, but not pull it). Arrow keys or the buttons move you.
S15.done: With the crates back in their marks, a narrow door appears behind them: a little back room. Inside: a woman's coat, hair ribbons, sewing thread, stockings, and a hatch in the floor with a fresh rope handle.

spots4.prompt: The chemical shelf and the balance (S8)

S8.title: The Chemical Shelf
S8.intro: The darkroom storeroom's stock ledger lists what each jar should weigh. Put a jar on the balance and add brass weights until the beam is level, then compare with the ledger.

jars.name: Silver nitrate
jars.why: The darkroom log: '40 g used for plate emulsion, 2 Nov.'

S8.question: Which jar is short, with nothing in the log to explain it?
S8.wrong: Check the darkroom log, Chief: one of the short jars has a perfectly good reason.
S8.scuffs: Behind the shelf, the floor is scuffed in an arc, as if the whole unit swings out. Cold air comes through the gap.
S8.done: The cyanide jar is a scoop short, and nobody logged it. The poison came from this building, not the doctor's bag.

S9.title: The Darkroom
S9.intro: Billie's four aerial plates from the 1931 search, never printed. Develop each one: expose when the enlarger's needle is in the green band, then pull it from the developer between 55 and 65 seconds. Each plate can be retried once.
S9.compare: Now compare your print of plate 4 with the official crash-report photograph of the same spot. Click everything on your print that isn't in the official one.

spots.name: Truck tracks that run in from the road, under the rescuers' footprints
A drag trail from the wreck to where the truck stopped
A stretcher-shaped bundle under a canvas, by the truck

S9.miss: That's in the official photo too.
S9.ruined: Ruined: the plate is black. You have one retry.
S9.lost: That plate is lost for good. Plate 4 still matters most.
S9.done: Someone drove a truck to the wreck before the rescue party got there, and carried something to it on a stretcher. Billie took these pictures in 1931 and never printed them. Maybe she didn't want to know.

S10.title: The Manifests and the Payout
S10.intro: The Marigold's last flight: six passenger cards, five death certificates and the insurer's payout list. First put the cards in seat order, then match each passenger to a certificate.
S10.payout: Insurer's payout: six claims, all paid in full, June 1931. Claim 4 paid to Pryce Transcontinental 'on behalf of the estate'. Pinned under it: a Meridian Air cheque for $10,000 to the clerk of the 1931 inquiry board, signed J. Ferreira-Blake.
S10.receipt: Clipped behind the payout list: a receipt for a post-office box in Reno, rented in the name of 'Mrs. E. Marsh'. Paid by P.T.A.
S10.question: Which passenger was paid for but never declared dead?
S10.wrongOrder: The seat numbers are on the cards, Chief.
S10.wrongMatch: Those don't match. Read the names carefully.
S10.done: Six aboard, five certificates. Seat four, C. Pryce, nineteen years old: paid out on, never certified dead. And Meridian Air paid the man who kept the inquiry's papers.

S20.title: The Last Call
S20.intro: Hobbs kept the wax cylinder of the Marigold's last radio call. It runs about three minutes. Scrub the needle through it and find the last words before it ends.
segments: Static, and the pilot reading his position.
Engine noise rising; the pilot says 'heavy weather, ceiling zero'.

voice.text: Daddy, I can see the ridge!
voice.speaker: (a young woman, faint)

S20.question: Whose voice is it?
S20.needMark: Find the voice first: scrub to it and mark it.
S20.wrongMark: Nothing but static and engine there.
S20.done: The last voice on the Marigold was a young woman's, calling for her father.

S22.title: The Locked Case
S22.intro: Doctor Lindqvist's leather case, locked, on the office floor beside his bag. You can ask him, get a warrant through Danny, or pick it.

routes.label: Ask Lindqvist to open it (needs his trust)
routes.ok: He looks at you for a long time, then unlocks it himself. "Ask me again when you know the whole truth."
routes.no: "Certainly not, Inspector. A doctor's case is private."

routes.label: Have Danny radio for a warrant (45 min)
routes.ok: Danny comes back with the warrant read over the wire. Lindqvist unlocks the case without a word.

routes.label: Pick the lock yourself (Danny won't like it)
routes.ok: Danny turns his back. "I didn't see this, Chief."

S22.springy: Springy. That pin isn't binding yet.
S22.broke: Snap. Too much tension: the pick broke.
S22.outOfPicks: No picks left. You'll have to ask him, or get the warrant.
S22.contents: A prescription book: two years of burn dressings, salve and a sedative, all shipped to 'Mrs. E. Marsh, Box 41, Reno'. A brown bottle of sedative is missing from its slot. Tucked in the lid, a list in small, careful handwriting: 'Ribbons. Stockings. Size 5 gloves. A blue coat.'
S22.done: Someone has been treated for burns, secretly, for two years. And a sedative is missing.

spots5.prompt: The tank gauges and fuel ledger (S16)

wacocap.name: The Waco's fuel cap
wacocap.prompt: Look at the Waco's fuel cap
wacocap.text: The fuel cap on the Waco's top wing is loose, with a big greasy thumbprint across it. Ox's, by the size of it: the fuel log says he put five gallons in her this morning. Nothing wrong here.
wacocap.note: The Waco was fuelled this morning (Ox's thumbprint on the cap). Nothing odd.

S7.title: Readied for Flight
S7.intro: Inside the Trimotor 'Marigold II'. Look at everything in the cabin and the cockpit, then decide what this plane was being made ready for.

items.name: A stretcher cot strapped to the floor
items.text: A canvas stretcher, bolted where three seats have been removed, with leather restraint straps at the chest and ankles.

items.name: Wool blankets and a pillow
items.text: Folded, new, still smelling of the shop.

items.name: A travelling trunk
items.text: A woman's trunk, labelled in Pryce's hand: 'E. MARSH, c/o Hotel Baur au Lac, Zürich'.

items.name: A hat box
items.text: Inside, a soft felt cloche with a veil. Something to hide a face.

items.name: A doctor's sedative kit
items.text: A leather syringe case on the seat by the cot, stamped 'Dr. M. Lindqvist'. One syringe is filled and capped.

items.name: The flight plan in the cockpit
items.text: Sable Flat to Zürich, by Lisbon. Depart 05:00, 18 November. Pilot: W. Strand. Passengers: 2. Signed C. Pryce.

S7.question: What was this plane being readied for?
options: Carrying cargo out of the country
A business trip for Pryce alone
A passenger who couldn't walk or sit, kept calm and lying down
S7.wrong: Look again at the cot and the straps, Chief.
S7.done: A stretcher, straps, a doctor's syringe and a trunk for a woman called E. Marsh. Pryce meant to fly someone out at five this morning, lying down and sedated. The pilot on the plan: W. Strand. Billie.

S11.title: Raking Light
S11.intro: Two charred sheets in the lounge fireplace, the ashes still faintly warm. Move the lamp around them: each line only shows when the light rakes across it at the right angle.

sheets.name: Sheet 1: cream writing paper
lines: By Saturday we shall be free of him.
I have the tickets. The 9.40 from Reno.
Not one more year in that house. V.

sheets.name: Sheet 2: a typed contract page
lines: ...findings of the inquiry into the loss of the Marigold...
...no fault attaches to the operator or its agents...
Signed: [a signature in a different ink, traced over pencil]

S11.question: What do these sheets show?
options: Vivienne planned to poison her husband with Julian
Vivienne was leaving her husband, and someone forged a signature on the inquiry
S11.wrong: Read the letter again, Chief. Free of him how?
S11.done: Vivienne was running away, not plotting murder: she had train tickets. And somebody forged a signature on the 1931 inquiry to bury it.

S12.title: The Blackout
S12.intro: At noon the hangar lights died. Two generators, five circuits. The hangar, the radio and the beacon must be on; nothing may be overloaded. Generator 1 can carry 5 units, generator 2 can carry 3.
S12.missing: The hangar, radio and beacon all need power.
S12.observe: Under the panel: the lightning arrestor is burnt black, and the reset lever is sticky with radio solder flux, not Ox's engine grease. Ox, behind you, says he fixed it. He didn't.
S12.done: Power's back. Lightning took the arrestor last night, and whoever reset it was a radio man: Hobbs. Ox claimed the credit, and that's a lie.

S13.title: The Cracked Mount
S13.intro: Four old engine mounts on the bench. Dye-penetrant test: spray the red dye, wait, wipe it off, then spray the white developer. Cracks show as red lines. Ox watches you.
S13.wrongStep: Wrong order: now it's a smeared red mess. Clean it and start again.
S13.question: Which mount has a real crack?
S13.wrong: Straight, parallel lines are just marks from the machine that made the part, Chief.
S13.ox: Ox stares at it. "I did what I was told. Mr. Pryce said pass it, so I passed it."
S13.done: The Marigold's number two engine mount was cracked, and Ox signed it off as safe.

S16.title: The Night Burn
S16.intro: Read each tank's dial gauge, write it in the ledger, and compare with yesterday's figures. The gauges read in gallons.
S16.log: Today's issues logged by Ox: Tank B 5 gal (mail plane), Tank D 10 gal (generator). Nothing logged from Tank C.
S16.question: Which tank lost fuel that nobody logged, and how much?
S16.wrongRead: Your reading doesn't match the needle. Look again.
S16.wrong: Compare each tank with yesterday AND with the issue log, Chief.
S16.done: Thirty-eight gallons gone from the Trimotor's tank overnight, unlogged: someone ran her engines for a long time. That bang at quarter to eleven was her backfiring.

S19.title: The Barograph Overlay
S19.intro: Hobbs's original barograph trace from May 1931 is on tracing paper. Slide it over the 'official' weather report's pressure chart until the time marks line up.
S19.report: OFFICIAL WEATHER REPORT, 14 MAY 1931. Pressure steady. Winds light. Clear by noon. Fit for flight.
samples: The quick brown fox: e e e (clean)
The quick brown fox: e e e (clean)
The quick brown fox: e e e (the e is chipped at the top)
S19.reportE: Under the magnifier, every 'e' in the report is chipped at the top.
S19.question: Which machine typed the false report?
S19.aligned: Lined up: Hobbs's trace drops like a stone at nine, a deep storm, while the report says 'clear by noon'. Someone typed a lie.
S19.done: The 1931 weather report was falsified, typed on Miss Quill's machine. The same chipped 'e' as the note under Pryce's door.

S21.title: The Stakeout
S21.intro: The keeper's log notes a glow from the hangar roof vent 'every evening at dusk'. From up here, with binoculars, you can see the whole field.
S21.early: It's too light yet. The log says dusk. Wait here until half past four?
S21.waitLabel: Wait at the window until dusk
S21.scan: Sweep the binoculars along the hangar roof. When you see the glow, say so.
S21.miss: Just dust and the dark roof.
S21.seeds: By the pigeon coop: seed bags labelled in a small, careful woman's hand: 'Tuesday. Not too much.'
S21.done: A faint lamp glows under the hangar roof vent at dusk, as if someone below the floor has lit a lamp for the evening. Your first sight of the 'ghost'.

S24.title: Tamsin's Shorthand
S24.intro: Danny fished these out of the kitchen stove in the Quarters this morning, half burnt: pages of Tamsin's private ledger, in her own cipher. Every letter stands for another. The first words are probably 'PAID'. The cipher uses a keyword alphabet.
S24.hint: Keyword alphabets: write the keyword without repeated letters, then the rest of the alphabet in order.
S24.wrong: That gives gibberish. Try a name you keep hearing.
S24.done: PAID 200 MONTHLY. W/R 31 STORM FALSE. She was being paid to keep quiet about the false 1931 weather report.

ghost12: Noon. Every light in the hangar dies at once, and somewhere under the floor a music box starts to play, slow and tinny. Then it stops. Danny, on the radio: "Chief? Did you hear that?"
